title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for type 1 diabetes and nerve pain.

HPI
The patient presents today for a scheduled follow-up regarding their management of type 1 diabetes mellitus. They report persistent tingling and numbness in the lower extremities. The patient describes the sensation as a constant "pins and needles" feeling that occasionally worsens at night. They have been on insulin for several years and report consistent adherence to their injection schedule. They deny any recent acute episodes of low blood sugar.

Medication List
Long-acting insulin.

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented. Physical exam reveals diminished sensation to light touch and vibration in the toes and first metatarsals bilaterally. Reflexes are diminished at the ankles. No acute skin breakdown or ulcerations noted.

Assessment
1. Type 1 diabetes mellitus: Stable on current insulin regimen.
2. Polyneuropathy: The patient exhibits symptoms of peripheral neuropathy. However, based on the clinical presentation and history, this condition is unrelated to diabetes.

Plan
Continue current insulin dosage. Monitor sensation in lower extremities. Follow up in three months for routine management.
explanations: The provider states the polyneuropathy is not diabetic: code each separately.
Polyneuropathy not due to diabetes is coded separately (G62.9 when no cause is specified).
Do not assign Z79.4 for type 1 diabetes; insulin use is inherent.

distractors.why: Provider documentation of no link overrides the presumption.
The polyneuropathy still needs its own code.
Z79.4 is not assigned for type 1 diabetes.
